keyTakeaways: 40 Halloween trivia questions split into three bands: 12 yes-or-no for ages 5–7, 14 multiple-choice for 8–10 and 14 harder ones for 11–13.
The moon is not full on Halloween 2026: it was full on 26 October at 04:12 UT and is about two-thirds lit on the 31st, per the US Naval Observatory.
Barn owls screech and hiss rather than hoot, and spiders are arachnids with two body parts, not insects.
A boomerang round of five repeated questions after a break follows Leonard and Deevy's 2020 finding that spaced retrieval beat re-study in preschool children.
48.3% of views of SubhSandesh pages happen on a phone, so each question is short enough to read straight off one.

faqs.question: Which Halloween trivia questions suit a 5-year-old?
faqs.answer: Yes-or-no questions work best for ages 5 to 7: is a bat a bird (no, it is a mammal), does a spider have eight legs (yes), or does a barn owl hoot (no, it screeches). Children can answer by shouting, holding up fingers or pointing at a drawing.

faqs.question: Is the moon full on Halloween 2026?
faqs.answer: No. The US Naval Observatory times October 2026's full moon for 26 October, 04:12 UT; by the 31st it has waned to a gibbous moon about two-thirds lit. On Halloween 2027 it is a thin crescent, about 5% lit, after the new moon of 29 October.

faqs.question: Do barn owls hoot?
faqs.answer: No. The Barn Owl Trust says barn owls screech and hiss. If you hear regular hooting at night in Britain, it is most likely a tawny owl.

faqs.question: Is a spider an insect?
faqs.answer: No. The Australian Museum classes spiders as arachnids, with two main body parts and eight walking legs. Spiders and insects both belong to the arthropods, the largest group of animals on Earth.

faqs.question: Did Halloween start in Ireland?
faqs.answer: Some kids' quizzes give Ireland as the single answer, but historians still argue over the origins. A 1919 book by Ruth Kelley records old Halloween customs in Scotland, Ireland, Wales, England and Brittany, which is why this quiz asks about customs rather than one birthplace.

faqs.question: How do you score Halloween trivia when kids are different ages?
faqs.answer: Send each question to the child it was written for first: 2 points if they answer alone, 1 point with team help. For the 11 to 13 questions, give half a point for a number within about 10% of the right one.

faqs.question: Why repeat questions at the end of a kids' quiz?
faqs.answer: In four experiments with preschool children reviewed by Leonard and Deevy in 2020, words recalled again after a gap were remembered better than words simply re-studied. A short boomerang round after a break uses the same idea.

faqs.question: How long does a 40-question kids' Halloween quiz take?
faqs.answer: About 30 minutes, by our estimate, if each question and its explanation take roughly 40 seconds. Under-8s may manage only the first 12, so stop when attention drops.

faqs.question: What did children carve before pumpkins?
faqs.answer: Ruth Kelley's 1919 Book of Hallowe'en describes children in Scotland hollowing out large turnips and carving faces lit by a candle. The pumpkin questions in this quiz stick to how the plant grows.

faqs.question: Which weekday does 31 October fall on in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. All Saints' Day follows on 1 November and All Souls' Day on 2 November.

faqs.question: Does SubhSandesh have a quiz tool for a kids' party?
faqs.answer: No. SubhSandesh makes one-person greeting pages, so its Halloween templates suit sending a card to the quiz winner, not running the game. The regular card has a Kids tone with no blood, gore or jump scares.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Trivia for Kids: 40 Questions by Age, Easy to Harder

These 40 Halloween trivia questions for kids come in three age bands: 12 yes-or-no questions for ages 5 to 7, 14 multiple-choice questions for 8 to 10, and 14 harder ones for 11 to 13. Every answer has a one-line reason from a named source, checked on 15 October 2026.

The questions are short on purpose: SubhSandesh hosts 5,199 personalised greeting pages, and 48.3% of their views happen on a phone, and a phone is how most parents read a quiz aloud. Below: the questions, a topic table, a way to run mixed ages, and when to use something else.

## What makes Halloween trivia right for kids?

Halloween trivia for kids is a set of short questions about the animals, plants, sky and customs of late October, pitched at what a child can see or reason out. Good answers are true, checkable and not frightening.

That rules out a lot of what ranks. Two ranking kids' quizzes we read on 15 October 2026 give "Ireland" or "Celtic" as the single answer to where Halloween came from, which historians still argue over. This set sticks to animals, pumpkins, the 2026 and 2027 moon, and customs printed in a dated 1919 book.

## 40 Halloween trivia questions for kids, in 3 age bands

Older children can play the younger rounds as warm-ups. Each answer names its source in brackets or a link.

### Ages 5 to 7: 12 yes-or-no and point-to-it questions

Read each aloud. Children shout yes or no, hold up fingers, or point at a drawing.

1. **Is a bat a kind of bird?** No. Bats are mammals, says [Bat Conservation International (BCI)](https://www.batcon.org/about-bats/bats-101/).
2. **Does a mother bat raise one baby a year, or ten?** One. Most species give birth to a single pup yearly (BCI).
3. **Hold up fingers: does a spider have six legs or eight?** Eight. Spiders are arachnids, not insects, per the [Australian Museum's spider factsheet](https://australian.museum/learn/animals/spiders/).
4. **Point to where a spider's silk comes out: front or back?** The back. Spinnerets sit on the abdomen.
5. **Can a spider chew its dinner?** No. It turns food into liquid with digestive juices, then sucks it up.
6. **Does a barn owl go "hoo-hoo"?** No. It screeches and hisses, says the [Barn Owl Trust](https://www.barnowltrust.org.uk/barn-owl-facts/); a hooting British owl is usually a tawny owl.
7. **Do bees help pumpkins grow?** Yes. They carry pollen from male flowers to female ones, per [Illinois Extension's pumpkin guide](https://extension.illinois.edu/pumpkins/growing-pumpkins).
8. **Can a pumpkin flower have a tiny pumpkin under it?** Yes. Female flowers sit on a small baby fruit; male flowers don't.
9. **Is every ripe pumpkin orange?** No. Most varieties ripen orange, but not all (Illinois Extension).
10. **Is the moon full on Halloween 2026?** No. It was full on 26 October; on the 31st it is about two-thirds lit, per [US Naval Observatory (USNO) moon-phase data](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/api/moon/phases/date?date=2026-10-01&nump=6).
11. **Long ago in Scotland, did children carve lanterns from turnips?** Yes. [Ruth Kelley's *The Book of Hallowe'en* (1919)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/20644) describes candle-lit turnip faces.
12. **Is the day after Halloween called All Saints' Day?** Yes. Kelley calls Halloween the eve of All Hallows, the saints' day on 1 November.

### Ages 8 to 10: 14 multiple-choice questions

Read the options twice. Teams agree on one letter before you reveal.

13. **"Chiroptera", the scientific name for bats, means:** (a) night bird (b) hand-wing (c) cave mouse. **(b)**, from Greek *cheir* and *pteron* (BCI).
14. **The world's smallest bat is the:** (a) bumblebee bat (b) vampire bat (c) flying fox. **(a)**, about 2 g fully grown (BCI).
15. **A giant golden-crowned flying fox's wingspan reaches:** (a) 30 cm (b) 1 m (c) 6 ft. **(c)**: 1.8 m, the largest bat (BCI).
16. **A Mexican free-tailed bat's top speed in short bursts:** (a) 10 mph (b) 40 mph (c) 100 mph. **(c)**, the fastest bat known (BCI).
17. **Spiders belong to the:** (a) insects (b) arachnids (c) reptiles. **(b)**, like scorpions and mites (Australian Museum).
18. **A spider's main body parts number:** (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 4. **(a)**: cephalothorax and abdomen.
19. **British barn owls mostly hunt:** (a) field voles (b) fish (c) berries. **(a)** (Barn Owl Trust).
20. **The heavier barn owl is usually the:** (a) male (b) female (c) neither. **(b)**: about 360 g against 330 g (Barn Owl Trust).
21. **On a pumpkin vine, the first flowers are:** (a) male (b) female (c) both. **(a)**, almost always (Illinois Extension).
22. **A male pumpkin flower stays open for:** (a) one day (b) one week (c) one month. **(a)**, then drops off.
23. **Northern gardeners plant Halloween pumpkins in:** (a) January (b) late May (c) September. **(b)**; the far south waits until early July (Illinois Extension).
24. **On Halloween 2027 the moon is:** (a) full (b) a thin crescent (c) half. **(b)**: new moon is 29 October, so about 5% is lit (USNO).
25. **"Lambs'-wool", a popular Halloween drink in the 1700s, was:** (a) milk with crushed roasted apples (b) hot chocolate (c) pumpkin soup. **(a)**, says Kelley.
26. **To the Welsh, November Eve was:** (a) New Year's Eve (b) harvest day (c) a king's birthday. **(a)**: Kelley's "Nos-Galan-Gaeof", the night before winter's first day.

### Ages 11 to 13: 14 harder questions with no options

Score one point per answer. Give half a point for a number within about 10%.

27. **How long did the oldest known bat, a Brandt's myotis, live?** At least 41 years (BCI).
28. **How many Mexican free-tailed bats gather at Bracken Cave, Texas, the world's largest bat colony?** Up to 20 million in summer (BCI).
29. **How many bat species are known?** Accept 1,400 to 1,500-plus: BCI's page prints both figures, because counts change as species are described.
30. **How far must a minnow's fin poke above a pond for a fishing bat to detect it?** About 2 mm, by echolocation (BCI).
31. **Spiders and insects share which group, Earth's largest?** Arthropods, with hard outer skeletons and jointed limbs (Australian Museum).
32. **About how many spider species live in Australia?** About 3,600, a few deadly to people (Australian Museum).
33. **Why don't a pumpkin vine's first flowers become pumpkins?** They are male; their pollen sets the bees' route before female flowers open (Illinois Extension).
34. **Record giant pumpkins and giant squash share which species?** *Cucurbita maxima*; they differ mainly in colour (Illinois Extension).
35. **When exactly was the October 2026 full moon?** 26 October, 04:12 Universal Time (USNO).
36. **When does the moon rise in New York on 31 October 2026?** About 10:59 pm EDT, after most trick-or-treating; in Delhi, about 10:28 pm IST (USNO).
37. **When does the crescent set in New York on Halloween 2027?** About 6:58 pm EDT, leaving the rest of the night moonless (USNO).
38. **What was hidden in an Irish Halloween supper of mashed potato, parsnips and onions?** A ring; Kelley says the finder would marry within a year.
39. **In Brittany, what was poured on graves on November Eve?** Milk, with candles set out to welcome dead relatives (Kelley).
40. **Which two church days follow Halloween?** All Saints' Day, 1 November, and All Souls' Day, 2 November (Kelley).

## The five Halloween trivia topics compared

The table splits the 40 questions by topic and band, with the source that settles each. Drop any topic that doesn't suit your group.

| Topic | Questions (5–7 / 8–10 / 11–13) | Source checked | Number children argue about |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bats and owls | 3 / 6 / 4 | BCI (Feb 2026); Barn Owl Trust (Aug 2026) | 20 million bats in one cave |
| Spiders | 3 / 2 / 2 | Australian Museum (reviewed Aug 2026) | 3,600 Australian species |
| Pumpkins | 3 / 3 / 2 | Illinois Extension (undated) | A male flower lasts 1 day |
| The moon | 1 / 1 / 3 | USNO, 2026 and 2027 | 5% lit on 31 Oct 2027 |
| Customs | 2 / 2 / 3 | Kelley, 1919 | 1 and 2 November |

Bats and owls carry the most questions because children already have opinions about them. Only the moon round dates, so recheck it after 2027.

## How to run Halloween trivia with mixed ages

Make teams of three or four, mixing age bands. Each question goes first to the child it was written for: alone earns 2 points, with team help 1. That stops one 12-year-old answering everything.

Then add a boomerang round. Reviewing four experiments with preschool children, [Leonard and Deevy (2020)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8084525) found that words practised by repeated spaced retrieval were recalled better than words re-studied or retrieved straight away, in children with and without a language impairment.

- **Boomerang round:** after a snack break, re-ask five first-half questions.
- **Pictures count:** the study also tested recall by picture pointing, so a pointed answer scores in full.
- **Timing:** about 40 seconds per question, roughly 30 minutes in all (our estimate).
- **Tie-breaker:** question 28; the closest guess to 20 million wins.

## Sending a Halloween card to the quiz champion

SubhSandesh does not run quizzes or invite groups. Its two Halloween pages greet one person, such as the champion.

The [interactive Halloween card with a Kids tone](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes and holds up to six photos. Its Kids tone is spooky-cute, with round blushing ghosts and no blood, gore or jump scares, and the No button waits as "maybe later?".

The [cinematic Halloween page with a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds up to 12 photos, an optional unlock time and a 280-character reply box; for kids the No button never appears. Since 38.5% of creators password-protect a page before sharing, add one to any page carrying a child's photos. For other occasions, the [full template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) lists every page type.

## When this quiz is the wrong choice

- **Toddlers:** we have not tested even the yes-or-no band on toddlers.
- **Children afraid of spiders:** drop questions 3 to 5, 17, 18, 31 and 32.
- **A film or sweets crowd:** there are no film or candy-brand questions.
- **Southern hemisphere groups:** the planting answers follow Illinois seasons.
- **A whole class:** our pages greet a single person, in English; print the questions instead.

## Sources

- Bat Conservation International, "Bats 101", updated 20 February 2026.
- Australian Museum, "Spiders", 11 October 2018.
- Barn Owl Trust, "Barn Owl facts", updated 24 August 2026.
- Illinois Extension, "Growing Pumpkins", undated.
- US Naval Observatory moon tables, 2026 and 2027, accessed 15 October 2026.
- Ruth Edna Kelley, *The Book of Hallowe'en*, 1919.
- Leonard and Deevy, Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 16 October 2020.
